chapters.title: Chapter 6 — Adding ing, ed, er
chapters.focus: adding ing, ed, er (no change to the root)
chapters.description: Children add ing, ed and er to a root word without changing the root, plus three Year 1 common exception words.

meaning.definition: Spoke words out loud.
meaning.example: She said hello to her teacher.

meaning.definition: Speaks words out loud right now.
meaning.example: My dad says it is time for tea.

meaning.definition: To put a question to someone.
meaning.example: I will ask Mum for a drink.

meaning.definition: Pushing yourself up off the ground into the air.
meaning.example: The frog is jumping into the pond.

meaning.definition: Did something nice to make a job easier.
meaning.example: Tom helped me carry the bag.

meaning.definition: Moving along on your feet.
meaning.example: We are walking to the park.

meaning.definition: Someone who colours pictures or walls with a brush.
meaning.example: The painter made the door bright red.

meaning.definition: Hit something with your foot.
meaning.example: She kicked the ball over the wall.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 — ai, oi, ay, oy
chapters.description: Children spell the sounds ai, oi, ay and oy, plus five Year 1 common exception words.

meaning.definition: The opposite of "yes"; you say it when you do not agree.
meaning.example: No, I do not want any more peas.

meaning.definition: To move from one place to another.
meaning.example: We can go to the shops.

meaning.definition: Very much, or for that reason.
meaning.example: The cake smells so good.

meaning.definition: Next to something, as in "by the fire".
meaning.example: The cat sat by the fire.

meaning.definition: Belonging to me.
meaning.example: This is my red coat.

meaning.definition: A long vehicle that runs on rails.
meaning.example: The train stopped at the station.

meaning.definition: The earth that plants grow in.
meaning.example: Seeds grow well in warm soil.

meaning.definition: To have fun with toys or games.
meaning.example: We play ball after school.

meaning.definition: A male child.
meaning.example: The boy rode his bike to the park.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 — Long vowel sounds
chapters.focus: a-e, i-e, o-e, u-e; ee and ea
chapters.description: Children spell long vowel sounds with a-e, i-e, o-e, u-e, ee and ea, plus five Year 1 common exception words.

meaning.definition: In this place.
meaning.example: Come and sit here next to me.

meaning.definition: In that place, not here.
meaning.example: Put your shoes over there by the door.

meaning.definition: In what place.
meaning.example: Where did you put my hat?

meaning.definition: A building where people live.
meaning.example: Our house has a blue door.

meaning.definition: Belonging to us.
meaning.example: We water our plants every day.

meaning.definition: A sweet food baked in an oven.
meaning.example: We ate a big cake at the party.

meaning.definition: A toy that flies on a long string.
meaning.example: The kite flew high in the wind.

meaning.definition: The place where you live.
meaning.example: I go home after school.

meaning.definition: A long hollow pipe or container.
meaning.example: Squeeze the tube to get some paste.

meaning.definition: A flat green part of a plant.
meaning.example: A leaf fell from the tree.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 — wh, ph and k
chapters.focus: wh, ph; k before e, i, y
chapters.description: Children spell wh and ph, and the letter k before e, i or y, plus four Year 1 common exception words.

meaning.definition: Someone you like and who likes you.
meaning.example: My friend came to play today.

meaning.definition: A place where children go to learn.
meaning.example: We read books at school.

meaning.definition: To place something somewhere.
meaning.example: Put your coat on the hook.

meaning.definition: To press something away from you.
meaning.example: Push the door to open it.

meaning.definition: A round thing that turns, like on a bike.
meaning.example: The bike has a flat wheel.

meaning.definition: A thing you use to talk to people far away.
meaning.example: Mum called Gran on the phone.

meaning.definition: A clever grey animal that swims in the sea.
meaning.example: The dolphin jumped out of the water.

meaning.definition: A baby cat.
meaning.example: The kitten drank some milk.

meaning.definition: A man who rules a country.
meaning.example: The king wore a gold crown.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 — Days of the week
chapters.focus: days of the week (Monday to Sunday)
chapters.description: Children spell the seven days of the week with their capital letters, plus three Year 1 common exception words.

meaning.definition: The first day of the school week.
meaning.example: We have music on Monday.

meaning.definition: The day after Monday.
meaning.example: I swim every Tuesday.

meaning.definition: The day after Tuesday.
meaning.example: We go to the library on Wednesday.

meaning.definition: The day after Wednesday.
meaning.example: Gran comes to tea on Thursday.

meaning.definition: The day after Thursday.
meaning.example: We have fish and chips on Friday.

meaning.definition: The first day of the weekend.
meaning.example: On Saturday we play in the park.

meaning.definition: The last day of the week.
meaning.example: We visit Grandad on Sunday.

meaning.definition: This very day.
meaning.example: I am six years old today.

meaning.definition: To bring something towards you.
meaning.example: Pull the rope as hard as you can.

meaning.definition: Holding as much as it can.
meaning.example: The jug is full of milk.
